methodological_questions: Does adherence to the recommended mix predict winning (series or game) beyond team quality?
Is the recommendation derived independently of the outcome and of the evaluation games?
Is 54 series enough power for a series-level rank or logistic test?
Are play-type labels and the suppression trigger reliable enough, given tagger floors and sparse trigger exposure?
How should adherence be defined and multiplicity handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning: game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008, but inflated n and confounded by team quality. Series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 at n=50, underpowered, with ~80 series stated as needed for p<0.05. The low AVOID-share bin won 52.6% vs 37.0% for the 25-50% bin. Recorded verdict: inconclusive; failure mechanism A_unanswerable; still confounded by team quality (OKC disciplined and good); no validation recorded.

BEST/AVOID run rates vs series wins in 55 series (n=110 series-directions). BEST ran on 44.7% of triggers (9.7% of volume), AVOID on 61.1% (23.3% of volume). Spearman BEST vs won rho=+0.131 p=0.1723; AVOID vs won rho=-0.098 p=0.3099, both not significant. INSUFF_EVIDENCE was 91.5% of triggers. Recorded verdict: null; failure type A_unanswerable; no validation recorded.

In holdout games, a mix closer to the model's recommended mix had higher efficiency. Raw gap +5.18 ORtg; strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg (+0.0193 vs -0.0134 PPP residual). n=908 game-team rows (454 games), no CI stated. Outcome is efficiency, not winning. Model regret is non-negative by construction. Validation was same-pipeline.

Descriptive conformance in single 2025-26 playoff G1s (4 games x 2 offenses). Average |delta| between observed and recommended mix ranged 4.5pp to 24.0pp across leverage buckets, and 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. CUT and PNR were muted by the tagger floor. No outcome comparison was made.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level AVOID share vs winning, with a game-level version.
failed_approaches.why: Series n=50 gave p=0.07 and was underpowered. The game-level significance came from inflated n and the team-quality confound (A_unanswerable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level BEST/AVOID alignment vs series wins (n=110 directions from 55 series).
failed_approaches.why: Spearman correlations were not significant (p=0.172 / 0.310). 91.5% of triggers had insufficient evidence, and the small sample limited the test (A_unanswerable).

evidence_establishes: Two earlier series-level tests of essentially this question (50 and 55 series) found no significant association between BEST/AVOID adherence and series winning. Both are recorded as untestable/inconclusive/null, not as adequately powered rejections.
Point estimates were small and directionally as hypothesised (BEST rho +0.13, AVOID rho -0.10 to -0.26). The AVOID-share estimate is the larger of these.

Game-level alignment with the recommended mix is associated with higher efficiency (+3.27 ORtg after strength control) in a holdout, supporting a plausible mechanism. The validation was same-pipeline, and efficiency is not winning.
Team-quality confounding and sparse trigger exposure are recorded obstacles at series level.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence predicts winning independent of team quality. No retrieved record controls for talent in a series-level win model.
Whether the null at n=50-55 is a true null. Power was inadequate, so it is not an adequately powered rejection.
Out-of-sample validity of the recommendation. The record for the efficiency finding is same-pipeline only, with no CI and no independent replication.
Whether the efficiency effect translates into game or series wins.
own_inferences: Adding a few series to reach 54 will not materially change power. The unit count is about the same as in the earlier null/inconclusive tests, so a repeated series-level test would likely reproduce an inconclusive result.
For rho≈0.26, power at n=54 is roughly 50-55%. For rho≈0.10-0.13 it is below 20%. Confirmation at series level is therefore unlikely.
A positive naive series-level result would be more likely a talent artifact than a real effect, because better teams are plausibly more disciplined and also win more.

If the 54 series include partial 2025-26 playoff series (that file is partial before 2026-06-21), outcomes could be incomplete or later change. That would risk lookahead and label instability, and the series count should be frozen after completion.
The efficiency-to-winning link probably exists but is small. Detecting it needs the game level with within-series or team-quality controls and cluster-robust inference, not series-level ranks.
uncertainties: How 'adherence' is defined here: the BEST/AVOID run share, the L1 distance to the recommended mix, or something else. This is not specified in the question.
Whether the recommendation was fit on games that overlap the evaluation series.
Which seasons the 54 series cover and whether any are in progress.
The tagger floor for CUT/PNR and the 91.5% insufficient-evidence trigger rate could make adherence unmeasurable in many series.
No independent validation of play-type labels is recorded.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, a straightforward series-level correlation test would look feasible. The records show two prior series-level attempts (n=50, n=55) ended untestable/inconclusive/null because of power and talent confounding, so repeating that design with n=54 is not worth running. The efficiency finding in SF-APPM-001 suggests a game-level, talent-controlled test as the viable alternative.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series gives about 50-55% power only for rho≈0.26, and much less for the smaller observed effects (rho≈0.10-0.13). The earlier record put the need at ~80 series.
Team quality drives both discipline and winning. Without a strength control, a series-level association cannot be attributed to adherence.
91.5% of suppression triggers had insufficient evidence in a prior study, so adherence is measured on few triggers per series.

prior_work.summary: Series-level versions were tested twice and left inconclusive/null, underpowered and confounded. Game-level alignment predicts efficiency, but with same-pipeline validation. No retrieved study tested whether adherence predicts winning with talent controls and adequate power.

risks.text: Series-level n=54 is underpowered for realistic effects. Game-level n is larger, but games within a series are correlated, so effective n is lower than the row count.
Team and opponent quality, home court, injuries and game state affect both adherence and winning. The game-level p=0.008 in SF-CHT-039 was attributed to this confound.
If the recommended mix is fit using the same series or games, or on data including the outcome series, adherence is partly outcome-derived. Playoff series in progress make this worse.

The 'recommended' mix may be derived from points scored. Adherence would then correlate with scoring by construction, which is a risk for the +3.27 ORtg finding in SF-APPM-001 (model regret is non-negative by construction).
Triggers are rare, and BEST/AVOID occupies only 9.7% / 23.3% of volume. Many series have little or no insufficient-evidence-free exposure.
The tagger floor mutes CUT and PNR, so some play types cannot appear in the observed mix and adherence is biased.
Adherence measures (share, L1 distance, rank-1 match) disagree, as in SF-APPS-017 where 4 of 8 sides matched opener #3, not rank-1. The play-type tagger has no recorded validation.
Several adherence definitions (BEST, AVOID, distance), levels (game, series) and thresholds invite forking paths.
Play-type behavior and suppression schemes may change across four seasons and from regular season to playoffs.

design.estimand: The association between a team-game's adherence to a pre-specified recommended mix (a continuous L1 distance to the recommended mix, computed only on triggers with sufficient evidence) and the game win (a point-differential secondary outcome). It is adjusted for team and opponent strength. The target is the within-series effect: does the team that adheres more in a given game win more often than the same team in other games of the series?
design.unit: Team-game within series (primary). Series-level (n=54) is descriptive only.
design.sample: The minimum viable test is the game-level analysis of the 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoffs and regular seasons as a training and tuning set, with the recommendation frozen before evaluation. The 2025-26 playoffs are the pre-registered holdout, analysed only after 2026-06-21 when the file is complete. Exclude games or triggers with insufficient evidence, and report the count excluded.
design.power: At series level, 54 gives roughly 50-55% power for rho=0.26 and far less for rho≈0.1. This is inadequate. At game level, the effective sample must be computed from series clustering. The study should proceed only if a simulation shows at least 80% power for the smallest effect of interest, for example a 3-percentage-point win-probability change per 1 SD of adherence. Otherwise report the result as untestable.
design.controls: Pre-game team strength (the regular-season net rating or an externally priced rating available before the game), opponent strength, home court, series fixed effects, rest, injuries/lineup availability, and score state. Clustered standard errors by series. The recommendation must be fit out of sample (leave-one-series-out or time-ordered) so that the recommended mix never uses the evaluated game's outcome.
design.falsification: Placebo adherence using a shuffled or opponent-mismatched recommended mix, which should show no association with winning. A negative-control outcome fixed before the game (pre-game team rating) should show no association with adherence once strength is controlled. Also check that the adherence-efficiency link does not vanish once outcome-derived components are removed.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis (the L1 adherence coefficient on game win, within-series). BEST share, AVOID share and series-level rho are secondary and reported with Holm correction. No other definitions are tested.
design.decision_rule: Call the hypothesis supported only if the strength-controlled adherence coefficient has a 95% cluster-robust CI that excludes 0 in the predicted direction on the 2025-26 holdout, with the same sign in the training seasons, and the placebo is null. Call it rejected only if the CI excludes the smallest effect of interest at 80% power. Otherwise report untestable/inconclusive. Do not run the series-level test as confirmatory.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, rotation, matchup and box-score files for 2022-23 to 2025-26. The 2025-26 playoff file must be frozen as complete (on or after 2026-06-21) with a recorded data hash. The recommendation model version and tagger version are recorded before evaluation.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether any more tool calls are worth it, but the budget is fine and I think I can finish without them. The series count is the thing to double-check: 54 series, with the 2025-26 playoffs only partly complete as of 2026-06-16, so the count may include unfinished series. The earlier studies used 50 and 55 series, which is worth keeping in mind.

I'm working through the playoff series count: 15 series for each of the 2022-23 through 2024-25 seasons gives 45, and the partial 2025-26 playoffs might add about 9, which would make 54. That's only my inference. I'm also noting that the SF-APPM-001 check is game-level and uses the same pipeline, with PPP as the outcome rather than winning, so it supports mix alignment predicting efficiency but not winning. Given that the series-level evidence has been null or inconclusive across 50 to 55 series, I'm leaning toward not proceeding with a series-level confirmatory test, and instead describing a minimal game-level, within-series design with fixed effects that would wait for the completed 2026-06-21 playoff data.

I'm estimating statistical power for the series-level test: with about 54 series, detecting a correlation of around 0.26 would reach only roughly 50 to 55 percent power, and the observed value of 0.13 would have very low power.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether any more tool calls are worth it, but the budget is fine and I think I can finish without them. The series count is the thing to double-check: 54 series, with the 2025-26 playoffs only partly complete as of 2026-06-16, so the count may include unfinished series. The earlier studies used 50 and 55 series, which is worth keeping in mind.

I'm working through the playoff series count: 15 series for each of the 2022-23 through 2024-25 seasons gives 45, and the partial 2025-26 playoffs might add about 9, which would make 54. That's only my inference. I'm also noting that the SF-APPM-001 check is game-level and uses the same pipeline, with PPP as the outcome rather than winning, so it supports mix alignment predicting efficiency but not winning. Given that the series-level evidence has been null or inconclusive across 50 to 55 series, I'm leaning toward not proceeding with a series-level confirmatory test, and instead describing a minimal game-level, within-series design with fixed effects that would wait for the completed 2026-06-21 playoff data.

I'm estimating statistical power for the series-level test: with about 54 series, detecting a correlation of around 0.26 would reach only roughly 50 to 55 percent power, and the observed value of 0.13 would have very low power.
